title: If Solid Happiness We Prize
description: If Solid Happiness We Prize in Tonic Solfa to MERIBAH, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Nathaniel Cotton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 625 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Contentment and Resignation”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Particular Metre (8.8.6.8.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MERIBAH; any other Common Particular Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: If so-lid happ-i-ness we prize, With-in our breasts the jew-el lies; Nor need we roam a-broad: The world has lit-tle to be-stow; From pi-ous hearts our joys must flow, Hearts that de-light in God.

lines: Within our breasts the jewel lies;
The world has little to bestow;
From pious hearts our joys must flow,
To be resigned, when ills betide,
This is the wise, the virtuous part;
This is that incense of the heart,
Thus through life's changing scenes we'll go,
Its checkered paths of joy and woe,
Quit its vain scenes without a tear,
Without a trouble or a fear,

licence: Public domain: Nathaniel Cotton died in 1788.
credits: Words by Nathaniel Cotton (1705–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MERIBAH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
